h3_prompt:
Subject — One and only one character: 黎黎隆, matching the registered LLL-MAIN-001 character reference. Preserve her long red hair, sharp competitive expression, white-gray-red modular mechanical armor, cyan functional signal accents, mechanical dragon-claw feet, and one continuous long segmented mechanical dragon tail. Keep her face, armor topology, colors, proportions, and tail structure unchanged throughout.

Movement — 0–2 seconds: she stands upright immediately before one existing narrow mechanical passage, both feet grounded, leading foot neutral, and the long tail aligned compactly behind her. 2–4 seconds: the existing passage door begins one single steady closing motion, creating the only problem. 4–6 seconds: instead of moving immediately, she holds for one brief calculating beat; only her eyes measure the shrinking opening and the leading foot turns slightly inward. 6–8 seconds: at the last safe moment, she commits her whole body to one quick sideways pivot, clearly crossing from the near side of the passage to the far side by at least one shoulder-width; both feet leave the original standing position and land beyond the gap in one continuous action, with the long tail following. 8–10 seconds: the tail tip arrives one beat late, lightly touches the closing edge, and deflects upward, forcing her to arrest her momentum sooner than intended; no injury and no extra action. 10–11 seconds: she remains fully upright beyond the passage with both feet planted, tail tip raised beside the edge, and her confident grin tightening into a brief surprised competitive smirk. Each interval changes only one story variable.

Scene — Use only the registered SCENE-05 mechanical-airport environment if Picture 2 is actually bound and confirms one existing readable narrow mechanical passage. Keep the same single scene and the same asset version for B1, B2, B3, 4090, B4, and B5. Do not invent people, crowds, figure-bearing screens, reflected doubles, extra doors, or new props. If the bound scene lacks the required passage, return binding_mismatch and do not redesign it.

Camera — 16:9 landscape, one continuous shot with exactly one motivated stable camera change and no cuts. From 0–6 seconds, hold a stable full-body wide composition that shows her complete silhouette, both feet, the entire tail, both passage edges, and the shrinking gap. From 6–10 seconds, execute one smooth lateral dolly with a restrained push-in following her sideways crossing; create clearly visible background parallax and change the framing from full-body wide to full-body medium-wide without cropping the feet, tail, or passage edge. From 10–11 seconds, stop the camera and hold the resulting medium-wide composition. No second camera move, no pan away, no orbit, no handheld shake, no cut, no transition, no split screen.

Lighting — Stable soft directional light with clean planes and edges. Preserve registered character colors and cyan accents. No sudden color shift, flicker, weather change, or dramatic relighting.

Atmosphere — Alert, playful, daring, and competitive. Her deliberate late commitment feels clever and unexpected, while the delayed tail contact shows how wanting to win too decisively complicates the clean finish. Keep the action continuous, decisive, and physically readable.

Audio — Continuous low mechanical-airport room tone and soft ventilation hum; one restrained passage-motor cue from 2–4 seconds; one light armor pivot from 6–8 seconds; one brief tail-edge tick from 8–10 seconds. Audio supports spatial movement, action timing, and the slight comic consequence only. No lyrics, no strong beat, no music-video cutting, and no audio event that creates a second stimulus.

Negative — no duplicate character, no second human figure, no split screen, no clone or mirror-double, no extra limbs, no text overlay, no watermark, no abrupt redesign, no second ten-yuan, no forced sheng-ke-bu main axis, no vertical final output, no crowd, no reflected person, no extra character silhouette, no detached tail, no extra tail, no tail turning into wings, no static pose for the entire clip, no fixed shot size for the entire clip, no missing lateral displacement, no second camera move, no cut, no transition, no second stimulus, no sudden lighting change, no injury.
